stimulus.text: I was soon put down under the decks, and there I received such a salutation in my nostrils as I had never experienced in my life: so that, with the loathsomeness of the stench, and crying together, I became so sick and low that I was not able to eat, nor had I the least desire to taste any thing. I now wished for the last friend, death, to relieve me…

books.section: British Empire in America: Growth and Conflict (1650-1750)

primary_sources: Olaudah Equiano, The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano (1789)

stem: Equiano's account is one person's story of the Middle Passage. What is the most important limit on using it as evidence about the Middle Passage as a whole?

options.text: It was written in 1789, after the transatlantic slave trade had already ended
options.misconception: Gets the timeline wrong; the slave trade continued for decades after 1789.

options.text: It describes only the Atlantic crossing itself, not life on the plantations
options.misconception: Names a scope that is not a limit; the question is about the crossing itself.

options.text: It was written by a sailor who had never crossed the Atlantic himself
options.misconception: Misidentifies the author; Equiano crossed as a captive, not as a stay-at-home sailor.

options.text: It shows one voyage vividly but cannot alone prove how typical that voyage was

rationales.general:
1. Name the source's strength. Equiano was there — a firsthand account of one crossing.
2. Name the limit. One voyage, however vivid, is a sample of one.
3. Ask what the question needs. 'The Middle Passage as a whole' means the pattern across thousands of voyages.
4. Weigh the other options. The trade had not ended in 1789, the crossing is the subject, and Equiano did cross.
Remember: a single vivid story proves what happened once — proving a pattern takes more than one story.
rationales.A: The slave trade had not ended in 1789 — Britain ended its trade in 1807. The date is not the limit.
rationales.B: The crossing is the subject of the question. Describing only the crossing is not a limit here.
rationales.C: Equiano was a captive on the crossing, not a sailor who stayed home. He was there.
rationales.D: One vivid voyage cannot by itself prove what was typical across thousands of voyages.
